sentences.show: In 1941, three warships sank in six months. One sailor survived all three. He was a cat.
At least, that's what the Royal Navy said. They called him Unsinkable Sam.
The story begins on the German battleship Bismarck, the most feared ship in the Atlantic.
In May 1941, the Royal Navy hunted her down and sank her. Of more than 2,000 men, only 115 survived.
Hours later, a British destroyer, HMS Cossack, found a black and white cat floating on a plank.
They named him Oscar, after the signal flag for "man overboard".
Five months later, a German submarine torpedoed Cossack. 159 men died. The ship sank. The cat lived.
So they moved him to the aircraft carrier Ark Royal, the ship that had helped sink Bismarck.
Three weeks later, Ark Royal was torpedoed too.
Rescuers found him clinging to a plank. "Angry, but quite unharmed."
The Navy decided that was enough. Sam retired to a sailors' home in Belfast, and lived until 1955.
But here's the catch. A cat named Oscar really was rescued from Ark Royal. The Bismarck part, nobody can prove.
And there are photos of two different cats, both called Oscar.
So was he the luckiest cat in history? Or just the best sea story the Navy ever told?
